source.title: Minimum Time for K Connected Components

teaching.hint: How does the number of connected components change as time increases, and what happens if you consider the edge events backward?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Increasing time only removes edges, so component count never decreases. Reversing the edge events turns deletions into unions, which are easy to track.
solution_outline.approach: Sort edges by removal time descending. Starting with n isolated vertices, add edges back with union-find. The first edge whose successful union would reduce the component count below k identifies the minimum feasible time; if none does, return zero.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before processing a time-T edge, union-find contains every edge with time greater than T and any time-T edges already processed. Its component count is exact for those restored edges; adding further time-T edges can only reduce it.
solution_outline.correctness: At the crossing edge's time T, that edge and all other time-T edges are removed, while all later-time edges are kept, leaving at least k components. At every t<T, the crossing edge and all previously restored edges are present, yielding fewer than k components; adding any other edges cannot increase the count. If no crossing occurs, even the original graph has at least k components, so time zero is feasible.
solution_outline.complexity: O(e log e + e α(n)) time to sort and union e edges, and O(n + e) auxiliary space, with n and e at most 100,000.
solution_outline.pitfall: Removing an edge on a cycle need not increase the component count; counting removed edges instead of successful unions gives the wrong threshold.

accepted_alternatives: Binary-search a time threshold and rebuild connected components from edges with later removal times at each probe; monotonicity makes this correct but less efficient.
common_wrong_turns: Count every removed edge as a new component
Treat edges removed at time T as present at T
source_fidelity_notes: Image-only examples were removed; inclusive removal timing, possible initial disconnection, isolated vertices, large time bound, and at-least-k requirement were stated explicitly.
